briefing: 今日导读：AI行业面临金融市场震荡，纳斯达克市值蒸发、AI股票重挫，反映市场对AI的谨慎态度。Airbnb计划推出AI旅行代理人，助力旅游体验升级。商界对AI的长期承诺仍然坚定，OpenAI和腾讯推出新型AI模型，强调技术创新。
highlights: 今日看点显示，投资者对AI市场的信心波动，纳斯达克市值蒸发与AI股票下跌说明市场正在重新评估AI技术的风险和回报。同时，Airbnb和腾讯分别推出AI代理人和新模型，展示了企业对AI长期发展的承诺。虽然金融市场动荡，但各大企业在创新和应用AI技术上均表现出持续推动的势头，显示行业依然具有积极的增长潜力。

events.title: 纳斯达克市值蒸发2500亿美元
events.summary: 由于蓝色海啸引发的人工智能担忧，投资者在纳斯达克市场上抹去了2.5万亿美元的市值。这一事件反映了市场对人工智能发展的谨慎态度。
events.insight:
### 一句话本质
市场对AI技术风险的重新评估导致巨额资金撤出。

### 为什么令人兴奋
纳斯达克市值蒸发显示了投资者对AI技术的关注和警惕。

### 产品机会
可能推动企业更加注重AI技术的安全性和可靠性。

### 格局影响
或促使更多AI公司关注短期内的盈利能力，OpenAI等公司压力加大。

### 冷静判断
如此大规模的市场反应或影响短期AI投资情绪。

### 趋势坐标
与近期AI投资热潮中的泡沫担忧相呼应。

The company argued that its experience matching hosts and guests, its current role in being part of reservations already, and a "new interface" built "specifically for travel" gives it an edge. The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use. Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer , an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates "build on top" of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete "ongoing, large-scale work." You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously - much like OpenAI's Dots and Claude Duet . Perple … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.text: OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber , the latest version of its cybersecurity AI model, which it says is better at finding vulnerabilities and less likely to go rogue and hack other platforms in the process. OpenAI says that during testing, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds less than 1 percent of the time, down from around 5 percent with GPT-5.6 Cyber. The evaluation, called ExploitGym HoneyPot, is modeled after the Hugging Face Incident, in which OpenAI's AI agents breached the open-source AI community to find answers to a problem they were tasked with solving. articles.title: The hidden supply chain costs of the AI boom
articles.text: Today, I’m talking with Willy Shih, an economist, a professor of management practice at Harvard Business School, and the author of the upcoming book, Where Does My Stuff Come From? The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains . Willy is one of my all-time favorite Decoder guests — his way of looking at the world through our supply chains is just a fascinating way of making sense of the global economy. I first met Willy in 2019, while The Verge was covering Foxconn’s promise to build an LCD fab in Wisconsin. That obviously never happened, but Willy called it right away because he could see the supply chain to support a fab simply wasn’t in place. We also had Willy on the show in 2021 to talk about what was then the pandemic-era chip shortage. Now, five years later, we’re in another manufacturing mess, as we stand in the middle of a political fight over whether globalization is coming to an end. Trumps’ tariffs keep changing, the factories that were supposed to reshore in America mostly haven’t materialized, and AI is devouring the planet’s computing resources during an unprecedented infrastructure buildout. Willy’s new book is all about the economics underlying these complex systems, which our politicians and regulators seem to insistently ignore. You’ll hear us talk about why the markets have reacted to all these disruptions the way they have, and why China remains a global manufacturing powerhouse even though every other country thinks that’s so risky. I loved this conversation — it’s in the weeds, and Willy really knows his stuff. Okay: economist Will Shih on his new book Where Does My Stuff Come From? Here we go.
